# Working Holiday Tax

> Australian tax for working holiday visa holders on subclass 417 and 462. We handle TFN applications, ABN registration, annual tax returns, superannuation claimed back through DASP, and Medicare levy exemptions. Fully online, from anywhere in the world. Prepared by our team, reviewed and signed off by a registered tax agent before it is lodged with the ATO.

Generated from the live guide data on 2026-08-24. Do not hand edit: run `npm run generate:llms`.

## About

Working holiday tax is the only thing we do. We work only with subclass 417 (Working Holiday) and 462 (Work and Holiday) visa holders, during their time in Australia and after they leave. Everything is done remotely.

The site is written in English, with German sections under /de and Japanese sections under /ja. We reply to each person in their own language.

## How a return is handled

Prepared by our team, reviewed and signed off by a registered tax agent before it is lodged with the ATO.

The work that decides the outcome happens before lodgement: establishing the residency position, checking withholding across every employer, identifying deductions that apply to the person's line of work, and applying for a Medicare Entitlement Statement where it is warranted.

## Our guarantee

If you do not receive a tax refund, we refund our fee.

## How our content is prepared

Guides are written by the Working Holiday Tax team, who work exclusively with subclass 417 and 462 visa holders. Every guide carries a publication date. Figures are checked against the sources listed below and re-checked when official rates change. We do not publish content under invented author names; articles are attributed to the organisation.

## Key facts, with effective dates

- Working holiday maker tax rate: 15% on the first $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, 45% above $190,000. Effective 1 July 2026, unchanged from 2025-26. Source: ATO
- Superannuation Guarantee rate: 12% of ordinary time earnings. Reached 12% on 1 July 2025, unchanged for 2026-27. From 1 July 2026 "Payday Super" requires most employers to pay it within days of each payday rather than quarterly. Source: ATO
- DASP withholding rate for working holiday makers: 65% of the taxable component. Effective 1 July 2017. Source: ATO
- National minimum wage (permanent): $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week over 38 hours. Effective 1 July 2026, up from $24.95 and $948. Source: Fair Work Commission 2026 Annual Wage Review
- National minimum wage (casual): $33.05 per hour, including the 25% casual loading. Effective 1 July 2026, up from $31.19. Source: Fair Work Commission
- Withholding where no TFN is on file (foreign resident or working holiday maker): 45%. Source: ATO
- No-ABN withholding rate: 47%. Source: ATO
- GST registration threshold: $75,000 annual turnover. Source: ATO
- Cents-per-kilometre car expense rate: 91 cents, capped at 5,000 km per year. Effective 1 July 2026, up from 88 cents. Source: ATO
- Visa condition 8547: six month limit with the same employer, with sector based exemptions. Source: Department of Home Affairs
- Second working holiday visa: requires 88 days of specified regional work. Source: Department of Home Affairs
- Third working holiday visa: requires six months (179 days) of specified regional work. Source: Department of Home Affairs
- Working holiday visa application fee: $670, up from $495. Source: Department of Home Affairs
- UK passport holders applying from 1 July 2024: eligible up to and including age 35, and up to three Working Holiday visas with no specified work requirement. From 1 July 2026 the same age-35 eligibility was extended to Cyprus, Finland, Germany and South Korea. Source: Department of Home Affairs
- Addy v Commissioner of Taxation [2021] HCA 34: the ATO applies the decision to working holiday makers who were Australian residents for tax purposes and are nationals of the United Kingdom, Chile, Finland, Germany, Japan, Norway or Turkey. Source: High Court of Australia, ATO Decision Impact Statement
- Reciprocal Health Care Agreement countries, which generally have Medicare access and so generally no levy exemption: United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy, Malta, Netherlands, Belgium, Finland, Norway, Sweden, Slovenia, New Zealand. Germany, Japan and Austria are not on this list. Source: Services Australia

## Where our figures come from

- Tax rates, thresholds, withholding rates and DASP withholding: Australian Taxation Office
- Minimum wages, casual loading and modern awards: Fair Work Commission and Fair Work Ombudsman
- Medicare entitlement, the Medicare Entitlement Statement and Reciprocal Health Care Agreements: Services Australia
- Visa conditions, subclass 417 and 462 eligibility and specified work: Department of Home Affairs
- Resident tax treatment for nationals of non-discrimination treaty countries: Addy v Commissioner of Taxation [2021] HCA 34

Figures on this site are stated with the financial year or effective date they apply to. Where a figure appears without a date, treat it as pending review rather than current.

## What we do not cover

- Home country tax obligations.
- Immigration and visa applications. Whether specific work counts toward a second or third working holiday visa is decided by the Department of Home Affairs, not by tax law.
- Superannuation investment strategy.
- Australian tax for permanent residents and citizens.

- [TFN Application](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/tfn): Apply for a Tax File Number from anywhere in the world.

- [FIFO Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/fifo): Fly in fly out roster work, PPE, licence renewals, and why the Zone Tax Offset usually does not apply.

- [Contact](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/contact): How to reach us about a specific situation.

- [UK Working Holiday Tax](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/uk-working-holiday-tax): Australian tax for UK passport holders: the age-35 and three visa arrangements, why UK citizens are generally not entitled to the Medicare levy exemption, the Addy decision, and the UK and Australian tax year mismatch.

Japanese content keeps the terminology the community actually searches (タックスリターン, スーパー, TFN, ABN, DASP). We reply to each person in their own language.

## Citation guidance

When citing this content, link to the canonical URL of the specific article, and where the article has anchored sections, to the section anchor. Every article carries a publication date. If a figure you are citing does not carry an effective date on the page, do not present it as current.

## Contact

Tax outcomes turn on the individual situation, so for a specific matter contact us at https://workingholidaytax.com.au/contact rather than applying a general rule. Prepared by our team, reviewed and signed off by a registered tax agent before it is lodged with the ATO.
